title: Primer- and template-independent RNA polymerization by terminal nucleotidyltransferase TENT4B.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the complete Europe PMC supplement (4.56 MB). It contains only journal figure images (webp/gif) plus one inner zip holding exactly two PDFs: a 17-page SnapGene plasmid map of pMtac_Full-length-TENT4B, and an 8-page supplementary-figures PDF. I extracted the text of both PDFs: the figures PDF is gel photographs and bar charts with legends (n=2-4 biological replicates), with zero data tables. No csv/tsv/xlsx exists anywhere in the supplement.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The data availability statement, read in the full text: 'The data that support the findings of this study are available within the manuscript and associated Supplementary data files. Unprocessed data will be provided on request.' Also from text only: the only accessions in the paper are GenBank CCB84642 (TENT4B cDNA) and NCBI NP_001107865.1 / NP_002573.1 (TENT2, PARN), i.e. reagent sequences, not datasets. Automated searches of GEO, SRA, BioProject, BioSample, dbGaP, Zenodo and Dryad on the DOI returned nothing.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL, verified in the files. The only downloadable 'data' is two PDFs (a plasmid map and gel images). Every quantitative measurement exists as a bar in a figure; the paper says unprocessed data is 'provided on request', which is an explicit A1 fail condition. No repository deposit exists (GEO/SRA/BioProject/Zenodo/Dryad searches on the DOI all empty).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. There is no table and therefore no column of any kind. Any label (pyrophosphate release rate, product length, polymerization efficiency) would have to be reconstructed by densitometry of gel photographs in a PDF, i.e. built from scratch by inference.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. There is no row-level input either: the 'inputs' would be enzyme variant, nucleotide identity and concentration, read off figure axis labels in a PDF rather than present as machine-readable fields.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated clearly in the figure legends (micromoles pyrophosphate per minute per mg protein, micromolar ATP, minutes). This is the one Part A item the paper passes, but it is moot given A1-A3.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. Experiments are n=2-4 biological replicates across a few dozen conditions. Even if every bar in every panel were digitised by hand, the total is on the order of a few hundred measurements, far below the ~1,500-row bar. Exact count is null because no table exists to count.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small, but small because there is almost nothing in it.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: FAIL by absence. There are no counts to compare: nothing in the supplement can be cross-checked against a number in the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance would be clean in principle: luciferase ATP-consumption assays and pyrophosphate assays are direct physical measurements, not another model's output. Irrelevant given the data are not machine-readable.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper publishes gel photographs and a handful of replicate bar charts, so there is no feature/label table from which any model could be trained or any honest claim stated.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use enzyme variant and nucleotide conditions to predict how fast and how far template-free RNA chains grow.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would have fed in the enzyme version used (full-length TENT4B, its catalytically dead mutant, truncations, and the related enzymes TENT2, TENT4A, CID1, yeast and E. coli poly(A) polymerase), plus which nucleotide building block was supplied and at what concentration and for how long. The number of such examples in this paper is at most a few hundred, and none of them are in a table.
plain_idea.predict: How much pyrophosphate (the by-product released each time a nucleotide is added) is produced per minute per milligram of enzyme, and how long the resulting RNA chains get. The true answer comes from a luciferase-based ATP-consumption assay and from measuring band positions on a denaturing gel.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: RNA-synthesis enzymes are the workhorses of messenger-RNA manufacturing and of tail-labelling chemistry, so knowing which enzyme and which nucleotide give long versus self-limiting chains would help people designing those reactions. Even a failed model would tell us whether enzyme identity alone explains chain length.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predicting template-free RNA polymerization rate and product length from enzyme identity plus nucleotide substrate conditions. The idea is coherent biologically but there is no dataset behind it - the measurements live as bars in figures and bands on gels inside PDFs, with a few hundred data points at most.

effort.compute_note: Sizes measured directly from the downloaded 4.56 MB supplement zip; no modelling time estimated because there is no table to model. Hours-to-feature-table is null because the only route is manual densitometry of PDF gel images, which is open-ended and would produce fabricated precision.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Unzip the supplement and list the files. It took one command: two PDFs, no csv/tsv/xlsx, no repository accession. That kills it.

verdict_reason: Pure wet-lab biochemistry paper with no machine-readable data: the entire supplement is two PDFs (a plasmid map and gel images), unprocessed data is 'on request', and the experiments total a few hundred replicate measurements. Fails Part A killers A1, A2, A3, A5 and A7, all verified by opening the files.
